name: Common Cold (Viral Upper Respiratory Tract Infection)
overview: A mild viral infection of the upper respiratory tract primarily affecting the nose and throat.
detailed_explanation: The common cold is caused by over 200 different virus strains, most commonly rhinoviruses. It causes inflammation of the upper respiratory tract membranes, resulting in congestion, sneezing, and runny nose. It is generally self-limiting and resolves within 7 to 10 days in healthy individuals.
causes_and_triggers: Infection with Rhinoviruses, Coronaviruses, or Adenoviruses
Droplet transmission from coughing or sneezing
Touching contaminated surfaces and subsequently touching eyes/nose/mouth
Weakened immune system or chronic sleep deprivation

medicines.name: Paracetamol (Acetaminophen)
medicines.purpose: Relieves mild fever, sore throat, and body aches
medicines.instructions: 500 mg every 4-6 hours as needed. Do not exceed 3000 mg in 24 hours.
medicines.precautions: Avoid taking with other acetaminophen-containing cold remedies to prevent accidental liver toxicity.

medicines.name: Pseudoephedrine or Oxymetazoline Nasal Spray
medicines.purpose: Decongestant to shrink swollen nasal passages and ease breathing
medicines.instructions: Nasal spray 2 sprays per nostril every 10-12 hours. Maximum 3 consecutive days.
medicines.precautions: Do not use nasal decongestant sprays for more than 3 days to avoid rebound congestion (rhinitis medicamentosa).

medicines.name: Cetirizine or Loratadine
medicines.purpose: Antihistamine to decrease histamine-mediated sneezing and rhinorrhea
medicines.instructions: 10 mg once daily with water.
medicines.precautions: May cause mild drowsiness in sensitive individuals; avoid alcohol.

remedies.name: Warm Saline Gargle
remedies.description: Dissolve 1/2 teaspoon of salt in 250ml of warm water. Gargle for 30 seconds, 3-4 times daily.
remedies.benefit: Reduces pharyngeal edema, thins mucus, and flushes irritants.

remedies.name: Steam Inhalation with Eucalyptus
remedies.description: Inhale steam from a bowl of hot water or facial steamer for 10-15 minutes.
remedies.benefit: Moisturizes dry nasal passages and loosens thick airway mucus.

remedies.name: Honey & Warm Lemon Infusion
remedies.description: Mix 1-2 teaspoons of natural honey and fresh lemon juice in warm water.
remedies.benefit: Coats and soothes irritated throat mucosa and acts as a gentle natural cough suppressant.

remedies.name: Abundant Fluid Hydration
remedies.description: Drink 2.5 to 3 liters of warm water, clear broths, and herbal teas daily.
remedies.benefit: Prevents dehydration and keeps respiratory secretions fluid.

recommended: Clear vegetable and chicken broths
Warm herbal teas (chamomile, ginger, peppermint)
Citrus fruits rich in Vitamin C (oranges, amla, kiwi)
Garlic and ginger infused soups
avoid: Very cold or iced beverages
Excessive dairy products if they make secretions feel thicker
Sugary sodas and deep-fried snacks
Alcohol and excessive caffeine

lifestyle_tips: Get at least 8 to 9 hours of restorative sleep to facilitate immune recovery.
Elevate your head with an extra pillow to ease nighttime nasal drainage.
Use a cool-mist room humidifier to keep indoor air humid.
diagnostic_tests: Clinical evaluation by doctor (rapid flu/COVID test if distinguishing diagnosis is needed)
emergency_red_flags: Fever higher than 102°F (38.9°C) lasting over 3 days
Shortness of breath or painful wheezing
Severe sinus pressure or forehead throbbing
Inability to swallow fluids

name: Influenza (Flu)
overview: A contagious viral respiratory infection caused by influenza viruses that attacks the throat, nose, and lungs.
detailed_explanation: Influenza is an acute respiratory infection caused by Influenza viruses (A, B, or C). Unlike the common cold, flu onset is typically abrupt and characterized by high-grade fever, severe myalgia (body aches), extreme fatigue, and dry cough. It can lead to complications such as secondary bacterial pneumonia.
causes_and_triggers: Infection with Influenza A or B viruses
Airborne droplet transmission from infected persons
Seasonal transmission spikes in winter months
High vulnerability among elderly, young children, and immunocompromised

medicines.name: Oseltamivir (Tamiflu)
medicines.purpose: Neuraminidase inhibitor antiviral drug that shortens illness duration and decreases complications
medicines.instructions: 75 mg twice daily for 5 days. Most effective when initiated within 48 hours of symptom onset.
medicines.precautions: Must be prescribed by a physician. May cause nausea or mild headache.

medicines.name: Ibuprofen
medicines.purpose: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory for reducing high fever and severe muscle pain
medicines.instructions: 400 mg every 6-8 hours with food. Do not exceed 1200 mg/day without medical supervision.
medicines.precautions: Take with meals or milk. Avoid if you have active peptic ulcers or kidney dysfunction.

medicines.name: Dextromethorphan
medicines.purpose: Cough suppressant for disruptive, exhausting dry cough
medicines.instructions: 10-20 mg every 4 hours or 30 mg every 6-8 hours.
medicines.precautions: Do not combine with MAO inhibitors or heavy sedatives.

remedies.name: Complete Bed Rest
remedies.description: Strict physical rest for 4-7 days to direct bodily energy toward fighting viral replication.
remedies.benefit: Accelerates recovery and prevents cardiovascular and pulmonary strain.

remedies.name: Electrolyte Rehydration Drinks
remedies.description: Drink oral rehydration solutions (ORS), coconut water, or diluted fruit juices.
remedies.benefit: Replenishes potassium and sodium lost through fever-induced sweating.

remedies.name: Lukewarm Sponge Baths
remedies.description: Wipe forehead, neck, and underarms with lukewarm (not cold) water sponge.
remedies.benefit: Helps safely dissipate heat during high-grade febrile episodes.

recommended: Warm chicken soup or lentil soup
Steamed oats, bananas, and applesauce
Ginger and turmeric milk or tea
Freshly squeezed orange or pomegranate juice
avoid: Hard-to-digest heavy meats and greasy foods
Caffeinated energy drinks
Sugary snacks and cold carbonated drinks

lifestyle_tips: Isolate in a well-ventilated bedroom to avoid infecting household members.
Wear a surgical or KN95 mask when leaving your room.
Disinfect frequently touched surfaces like doorknobs and phones.
emergency_red_flags: Difficulty breathing or chest tightness
Bluish lips or fingertips (cyanosis)
Confusion, dizziness, or sudden lethargy
Fever that improves and then returns worse with productive purulent cough

name: COVID-19 (SARS-CoV-2)
overview: A respiratory illness caused by the novel coronavirus SARS-CoV-2, ranging from mild cold-like symptoms to severe pneumonia.
detailed_explanation: COVID-19 affects the respiratory tract and vascular endothelium. Classic hallmarks include loss of taste (ageusia) or smell (anosmia), dry cough, fever, shortness of breath, and prolonged fatigue. Some variants also present with gastrointestinal distress and conjunctivitis.
causes_and_triggers: Infection with SARS-CoV-2 virus via aerosol particles and droplets
Close contact in indoor poorly ventilated crowded environments
Transmission before or without visible symptom onset

medicines.name: Paxlovid (Nirmatrelvir / Ritonavir)
medicines.purpose: Antiviral combination for high-risk patients to halt viral replication
medicines.instructions: Taken orally twice daily for 5 days within 5 days of symptom onset as guided by doctor.
medicines.precautions: Has multiple major drug interactions (e.g. statins, blood thinners). Strict doctor supervision mandatory.

medicines.name: Paracetamol & Ibuprofen
medicines.purpose: Symptomatic control of fever, headache, and myalgias
medicines.instructions: Paracetamol 650mg every 6 hours as needed.
medicines.precautions: Keep hydrated; monitor temperature.

remedies.name: Prone Position Breathing (Proning)
remedies.description: Lying face down on your stomach with pillows under neck, hips, and lower legs for 30-60 minutes.
remedies.benefit: Improves alveolar ventilation and lung oxygenation distribution.

remedies.name: Pulse Oximeter Monitoring
remedies.description: Check SpO2 oxygen saturation level every 4 to 6 hours on an index finger.
remedies.benefit: Enables early detection of 'silent hypoxia' (SpO2 dropping below 94%).

remedies.name: Steam & Saline Nasal Irrigation
remedies.description: Daily saline nasal rinse to reduce viral load in upper mucosal pathways.
remedies.benefit: Clears nasal passages and dampens localized irritation.

recommended: High-protein foods (eggs, pulses, fish, tofu) for tissue repair
Warm turmeric golden milk with black pepper
Zinc and Vitamin D rich foods (nuts, fortified grains)
Lots of warm water and clear broths
avoid: Ultra-processed foods
High-sugar confections
Cold processed meats
Alcohol

lifestyle_tips: Isolate for a minimum of 5 days or until 24 hours fever-free without antipyretics.
Practice deep breathing exercises (spirometry or pursed-lip breathing).
Keep the room well-ventilated with open windows or HEPA air filters.
emergency_red_flags: SpO2 oxygen saturation falling below 93%
Severe persistent pain or pressure in chest
Inability to stay awake or new onset confusion
Pale, gray, or blue skin, lips, or nail beds

name: Acute Gastroenteritis (Stomach Flu / Food Poisoning)
overview: An inflammation of the stomach and intestines causing diarrhea, cramps, nausea, and vomiting.
detailed_explanation: Acute gastroenteritis is an irritation and inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract caused by viral infections (Norovirus, Rotavirus), bacteria (Salmonella, E. coli, Campylobacter), or toxins in spoiled food. The predominant risk is rapid dehydration and electrolyte depletion.
causes_and_triggers: Consumption of contaminated food or water
Fecal-oral transmission through unwashed hands
Under-cooked meat, unpasteurized milk, or contaminated shellfish
Close contact with an infected person

medicines.name: Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS - WHO formulation)
medicines.purpose: Restores vital electrolytes (sodium, potassium, glucose) lost in stools
medicines.instructions: Dissolve 1 sachet in 1 liter of clean drinking water; sip continuously after each loose stool.
medicines.precautions: Do not mix with milk or sugary sodas. Must consume within 24 hours of preparation.

medicines.name: Ondansetron
medicines.purpose: Antiemetic to stop intractable vomiting and allow oral fluid intake
medicines.instructions: 4-8 mg orally or disintegrating tablet as prescribed by physician.
medicines.precautions: Do not use without medical advice; can cause constipation and headache.

medicines.name: Racecadotril or Loperamide
medicines.purpose: Antisecretory / antimotility agent to reduce stool frequency
medicines.instructions: Follow exact packaging or doctor directions.
medicines.precautions: NEVER take antimotility drugs like Loperamide if there is high fever or blood/mucus in stool (dysentery).

remedies.name: The BRAT Diet Protocol
remedies.description: Gradually reintroduce Bananas, Rice (white), Applesauce, and Toast once vomiting stops.
remedies.benefit: Bland, low-fiber foods that firm up stool and are gentle on the gastric lining.

remedies.name: Ginger or Peppermint Tea
remedies.description: Steep fresh ginger root in boiling water for 10 minutes and sip slowly when warm.
remedies.benefit: Natural carminative and 5-HT3 receptor blocker that suppresses nausea and spasms.

remedies.name: Electrolyte Coconut Water
remedies.description: Sip fresh green coconut water slowly in small sips.
remedies.benefit: Provides potassium, magnesium, and natural hydration.

recommended: Clear broths and congee (rice porridge)
Boiled potatoes without butter
Plain crackers and toasted white bread
Diluted chamomile or ginger tea
avoid: Dairy products (milk, cheese, ice cream) due to temporary secondary lactose intolerance
Fatty, greasy, or spicy foods
Coffee and acidic fruit juices (orange, tomato)
High-sugar foods

lifestyle_tips: Wash hands thoroughly with soap for at least 20 seconds before touching food.
Do not prepare food for other household members until 48 hours after symptoms clear.
Rest your stomach for 1-2 hours immediately after vomiting before attempting small sips of water.
diagnostic_tests: Serum electrolytes and kidney function test
emergency_red_flags: Signs of severe dehydration: no urination for >8 hours, sunken eyes, extreme dizziness upon standing
Stool contains visible blood or is black/tarry
Inability to keep any liquids down for more than 24 hours
High fever above 102°F accompanying diarrhea

name: GERD (Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease)
overview: A chronic digestive condition where stomach acid or bile repeatedly flows back into the esophagus.
detailed_explanation: Gastroesophageal reflux disease occurs when the lower esophageal sphincter (LES) weakens or relaxes abnormally, allowing corrosive gastric acid and pepsin to back up into the sensitive esophageal lining. Chronic irritation can lead to esophagitis, strictures, or Barrett's esophagus.
causes_and_triggers: Hiatal hernia or weak lower esophageal sphincter
Obesity or excessive abdominal pressure
Late-night heavy meals right before sleeping
Trigger foods: coffee, chocolate, citrus, tomatoes, garlic, mint, and alcohol

medicines.name: Omeprazole or Pantoprazole (Proton Pump Inhibitors)
medicines.purpose: Significantly decreases stomach acid production and allows esophageal tissue to heal
medicines.instructions: 20-40 mg once daily taken 30 to 60 minutes before the first meal of the day.
medicines.precautions: Long-term usage should be supervised by a physician to monitor calcium and B12 levels.

medicines.name: Antacids (Magnesium Hydroxide / Aluminum Hydroxide)
medicines.purpose: Fast-acting neutralization of existing stomach acid for acute burning relief
medicines.instructions: Chew 1-2 tablets or take 10-20 ml liquid as needed 1 hour after meals and at bedtime.
medicines.precautions: Provides only temporary relief; avoid excessive doses if you have kidney disease.

medicines.name: Famotidine (H2 Blocker)
medicines.purpose: Reduces nighttime gastric acid secretion
medicines.instructions: 20 mg once or twice daily 30 minutes before food or bed.
medicines.precautions: Consult physician for usage longer than 2 weeks.

remedies.name: Head of Bed Elevation
remedies.description: Elevate the head of your bed 6 to 8 inches using wooden bed risers or a wedge pillow (do not just stack normal pillows).
remedies.benefit: Uses gravity to prevent gastric acid from climbing up into the esophagus while asleep.

remedies.name: Chewing Sugar-Free Gum
remedies.description: Chew sugar-free gum for 30 minutes following meals.
remedies.benefit: Stimulates saliva production, which contains bicarbonate to neutralize esophageal acid.

remedies.name: Aloe Vera Juice
remedies.description: Drink 2 ounces (60 ml) of food-grade purified aloe vera juice before meals.
remedies.benefit: Soothes irritated mucosal lining and reduces inflammatory sensations.

recommended: Oatmeal, whole grains, and brown rice
Non-citrus fruits (melons, bananas, pears)
Lean poultry, baked fish, and egg whites
Green vegetables (broccoli, asparagus, green beans)
avoid: Fried, greasy, or deep-fried foods
Citrus fruits (lemons, oranges, grapefruit) and tomatoes
Chocolate, peppermint, and spearmint
Carbonated beverages, alcohol, and dark roast coffee

lifestyle_tips: Stop eating at least 3 to 4 hours before lying down to sleep.
Eat smaller, more frequent meals rather than large, heavy dinners.
Avoid tight-fitting waistbands or tight belts that press into your abdomen.
Maintain a healthy weight to reduce intra-abdominal pressure.
emergency_red_flags: Crushing chest pain radiating to arm, neck, or jaw (may mimic a heart attack - seek emergency care immediately)
Difficulty swallowing food (dysphagia) or feeling food get stuck in the esophagus
Vomiting coffee-ground material or red blood
Unexplained weight loss

name: Migraine Headache
overview: A neurological condition characterized by intense, throbbing unilateral head pain often accompanied by visual sensory changes.
detailed_explanation: Migraines involve neurovascular dysregulation characterized by trigeminovascular system activation, cortical spreading depression, and release of inflammatory neuropeptides such as CGRP. About one-third of sufferers experience a sensory 'aura' (flashing lights, blind spots) prior to the headache phase.
causes_and_triggers: Fluctuating hormones (especially estrogen shifts)
Dietary triggers: aged cheeses, wine, monosodium glutamate (MSG), aspartame, chocolate
Sensory overstimulation: bright or flashing lights, loud noises, pungent perfumes
Irregular sleep patterns, skipped meals, emotional stress or weather barometric shifts

medicines.name: Sumatriptan / Rizatriptan (Triptans)
medicines.purpose: Specific 5-HT1B/1D receptor agonist that constricts dilated cranial blood vessels and halts migraine attack
medicines.instructions: Take 1 tablet at the earliest onset of headache. A second dose may be taken after 2 hours if pain returns (max 200mg/day).
medicines.precautions: Contraindicated in patients with uncontrolled hypertension, coronary artery disease, or history of stroke.

medicines.name: Naproxen Sodium or Ibuprofen
medicines.purpose: NSAID to dampen neurogenic inflammatory pathways
medicines.instructions: 500 mg Naproxen at onset of symptoms with a large glass of water.
medicines.precautions: Take with food to protect gastric mucosa.

medicines.name: Combination Aspirin + Acetaminophen + Caffeine (Excedrin)
medicines.purpose: Synergistic pain relief and enhanced analgesic absorption via caffeine
medicines.instructions: 2 tablets at the start of symptoms. Do not take close to bedtime.
medicines.precautions: Avoid overuse (maximum 2-3 days a week) to prevent medication overuse headaches (rebound headaches).

remedies.name: Dark, Quiet Room Isolation
remedies.description: Lie down in a pitch-black, noise-free room with eyes closed for 1 to 2 hours.
remedies.benefit: Eliminates sensory input that overstimulates an already hyper-sensitized trigeminal nerve.

remedies.name: Cold Ice Pack on Forehead / Neck
remedies.description: Apply a cold gel pack wrapped in a cloth across the forehead or the base of the skull for 15 minutes.
remedies.benefit: Causes local vasoconstriction and numbs burning vascular throbbing.

remedies.name: Magnesium Glycinate & Riboflavin (B2)
remedies.description: 400-600 mg of magnesium glycinate and 400 mg Riboflavin daily for migraine prevention.
remedies.benefit: Regulates cortical neuron excitability and mitochondrial energy production.

recommended: Hydration with mineral water containing magnesium
Spinach, kale, pumpkin seeds, and almonds
Ginger tea (acts on inflammatory prostaglandins)
Consistent balanced meals at regular fixed hours
avoid: Aged cheeses and cured deli meats (tyramine)
Red wine and fermented alcoholic beverages
Artificial sweeteners (aspartame) and excessive MSG
Skipping breakfast or fasting for prolonged hours

lifestyle_tips: Maintain a consistent sleep-wake schedule, even on weekends.
Keep a detailed Migraine Diary to log foods, weather, and emotional triggers.
Practice progressive muscle relaxation or mindfulness meditation.
diagnostic_tests: Brain MRI or CT Scan (to rule out secondary causes if atypical symptoms occur)
emergency_red_flags: Sudden, explosive 'thunderclap' headache reaching maximum peak within 60 seconds
Headache accompanied by high fever, stiff neck, confusion, seizures, or double vision
Headache accompanied by numbness, weakness on one side of the face or body, or speech slurring
First severe headache occurring after age 50

name: Bronchial Asthma
overview: A chronic inflammatory disorder of the airways causing recurring episodes of wheezing, breathlessness, and coughing.
detailed_explanation: Asthma is characterized by bronchial hyper-responsiveness, chronic airway mucosal inflammation, and reversible bronchospasm. When exposed to allergens, cold air, or physical exertion, the smooth muscles surrounding the bronchi contract, mucus production surges, and the lumen narrows significantly.
causes_and_triggers: Airborne allergens: pollen, dust mites, mold spores, pet dander
Respiratory viral infections (rhinovirus, RSV)
Cold dry air or sudden weather shifts
Air pollutants, tobacco smoke, chemical fumes, and vigorous exercise

medicines.name: Albuterol / Salbutamol (SABA Inhaler)
medicines.purpose: Fast-acting rescue bronchodilator to instantly open constricted airways during an asthma flare
medicines.instructions: 1-2 puffs via spacer every 4-6 hours as needed for acute shortness of breath or wheeze.
medicines.precautions: Always carry this rescue inhaler with you. If you need it more than twice weekly, your asthma is poorly controlled.

medicines.name: Fluticasone or Budesonide (Inhaled Corticosteroid)
medicines.purpose: Daily maintenance controller to suppress underlying chronic bronchial inflammation
medicines.instructions: 1-2 puffs inhaled twice daily consistently, regardless of whether symptoms are present.
medicines.precautions: Rinse mouth and gargle with water after each use to prevent oral thrush (candidiasis).

medicines.name: Montelukast (Leukotriene Receptor Antagonist)
medicines.purpose: Oral tablet blocking leukotriene-mediated airway constriction and allergic response
medicines.instructions: 10 mg taken orally once daily in the evening.
medicines.precautions: Report any unusual behavioral or mood changes to your physician.

remedies.name: Pursed-Lip Breathing Technique
remedies.description: Inhale slowly through your nose for 2 seconds, then pucker lips as if blowing a candle and exhale for 4 seconds.
remedies.benefit: Maintains positive end-expiratory pressure in the airways, preventing collapse and trapping of air.

remedies.name: Peak Flow Meter Monitoring
remedies.description: Blow forcefully into a handheld peak expiratory flow (PEF) meter every morning.
remedies.benefit: Detects early bronchial narrowing hours before noticeable wheezing begins.

remedies.name: Warm Humidified Air & Hydration
remedies.description: Sit in a bathroom with a warm shower running or drink warm herbal infusions.
remedies.benefit: Liquefies tenacious bronchial mucous plugs.

recommended: Foods rich in Vitamin C and E (berries, spinach, bell peppers)
Omega-3 fatty acids (flaxseeds, walnuts, salmon) to reduce systemic inflammation
Magnesium-rich foods (seeds, leafy greens)
Ample warm water
avoid: Sulfite-containing foods (dried fruits, wine, processed pickled foods)
Foods causing gas and severe bloating that push up against diaphragm
Known personal food allergens (e.g. shellfish, peanuts)

lifestyle_tips: Use dust-mite proof encasings on pillows and mattresses.
Run a high-efficiency HEPA air purifier in your bedroom.
Wear a warm scarf covering nose and mouth when going out into freezing winter air.
Never smoke, and strictly avoid secondhand cigarette smoke.
diagnostic_tests: Spirometry with Pre- and Post-Bronchodilator Reversibility
emergency_red_flags: Rescue inhaler provides zero relief or relief lasts less than 2 hours
Severe breathlessness: unable to speak in full sentences without gasping
Intercostal retractions (skin sucking in around ribs and neck during inhalation)
Blue or gray lips, tongue, or fingernails

name: Hypertension (High Blood Pressure)
overview: A common condition where the long-term force of the blood against artery walls is elevated enough to cause health problems.
detailed_explanation: Hypertension is often dubbed the 'silent killer' because it commonly produces zero symptoms until significant vascular damage has accumulated. Blood pressure persistently at or above 130/80 mmHg strains the heart, hardens arteries, and drastically increases the risk of stroke, myocardial infarction, and kidney failure.
causes_and_triggers: High dietary sodium intake (>2300 mg/day)
Sedentary lifestyle and excess body weight
Chronic stress and tobacco consumption
Genetic predisposition and age-related arterial stiffness

medicines.name: Amlodipine (Calcium Channel Blocker)
medicines.purpose: Relaxes and dilates peripheral arterial smooth muscle cells to decrease blood pressure
medicines.instructions: 5-10 mg orally once daily in the morning or evening.
medicines.precautions: May cause peripheral ankle edema; discuss with physician if swelling occurs.

medicines.name: Telmisartan or Losartan (ARBs)
medicines.purpose: Blocks Angiotensin II receptors, preventing vascular constriction and protecting kidneys
medicines.instructions: 40-80 mg once daily.
medicines.precautions: Contraindicated in pregnancy. Regular monitoring of serum potassium and creatinine required.

medicines.name: Hydrochlorothiazide (Thiazide Diuretic)
medicines.purpose: Helps kidneys excrete excess water and sodium through urine
medicines.instructions: 12.5-25 mg taken in the morning to prevent nighttime urination.
medicines.precautions: Monitor blood electrolytes periodically.

remedies.name: DASH Diet Adoption
remedies.description: Adopt the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension eating plan rich in potassium, calcium, and magnesium.
remedies.benefit: Proven in clinical trials to lower systolic BP by 8-14 mmHg within weeks.

remedies.name: Sodium Restriction (<1500mg/day)
remedies.description: Stop adding table salt to food; eliminate canned soups, chips, and processed meats.
remedies.benefit: Decreases extracellular fluid volume and reduces vascular resistance.

remedies.name: Daily 30-Minute Aerobic Walking
remedies.description: Engage in brisk walking, cycling, or swimming 5 days per week.
remedies.benefit: Improves endothelial nitric oxide synthesis and arterial elasticity.

recommended: Potassium-rich foods (bananas, sweet potatoes, spinach, avocados)
Beetroot juice (high in dietary nitrates)
Garlic and hibiscus tea
Unsalted almonds, chia seeds, and oats
avoid: Pickles, papads, soy sauce, and processed sausages
Canned meals with high sodium preservatives
Excessive alcohol and energy drinks
Foods high in saturated trans fats

lifestyle_tips: Check blood pressure at home twice daily (morning and evening) with a validated arm cuff.
Practice slow, rhythmic deep breathing (6 breaths per minute) for 10 minutes daily.
Limit alcohol intake to under 1 standard drink per day or abstain completely.
Achieve and maintain a healthy body mass index (BMI 18.5 - 24.9).
emergency_red_flags: Hypertensive crisis: Blood pressure over 180/120 mmHg
Severe chest pain or shortness of breath
Sudden numbness or paralysis in face, arms, or speech impediment
Severe visual disturbance or sudden blindness

name: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
overview: A metabolic disorder characterized by high blood glucose levels resulting from insulin resistance and progressive insulin deficiency.
detailed_explanation: In Type 2 Diabetes, target tissues (skeletal muscle, liver, adipose) exhibit diminished responsiveness to insulin. As pancreatic beta cells fail to keep pace with demand, chronic hyperglycemia ensues, which over time damages microvascular (eyes, kidneys, nerves) and macrovascular (heart, brain) systems.
causes_and_triggers: Peripheral insulin resistance associated with visceral obesity
Lack of regular physical activity and sedentary screen habits
Diets high in refined carbohydrates, fructose corn syrup, and processed sugars
Strong familial genetic history

medicines.name: Metformin
medicines.purpose: First-line oral antidiabetic that reduces hepatic glucose production and enhances insulin sensitivity
medicines.instructions: 500-1000 mg taken with or after evening dinner to minimize GI side effects.
medicines.precautions: Must monitor kidney function (eGFR). Inform doctor before undergoing contrast CT scans.

medicines.name: Empagliflozin / Dapagliflozin (SGLT-2 Inhibitors)
medicines.purpose: Promotes excretion of excess glucose via urine while protecting heart and kidneys
medicines.instructions: 10-25 mg taken once daily in the morning.
medicines.precautions: Maintain good personal genital hygiene to prevent fungal urinary infections.

medicines.name: Glimepiride (Sulfonylurea)
medicines.purpose: Stimulates pancreatic beta-cells to secrete more insulin
medicines.instructions: 1-2 mg taken immediately before the first main meal.
medicines.precautions: Risk of hypoglycemia (low blood sugar); always carry fast-acting glucose tablets or candies.

remedies.name: Low Glycemic Index (GI) Meal Planning
remedies.description: Replace white rice, refined bread, and sugar with steel-cut oats, legumes, quinoa, and non-starchy vegetables.
remedies.benefit: Prevents rapid post-prandial glycemic spikes.

remedies.name: Post-Meal 15-Minute Walks
remedies.description: Take a gentle 15-minute walk immediately following lunch and dinner.
remedies.benefit: Muscle contractions transport glucose out of the bloodstream via GLUT4 translocation independently of insulin.

remedies.name: Fenugreek Seed Water
remedies.description: Soak 1 teaspoon of fenugreek seeds in a glass of water overnight; drink in the morning on an empty stomach.
remedies.benefit: Contains soluble galactomannan fiber that slows carbohydrate absorption.

recommended: Leafy greens, bitter gourd (karela), broccoli, and cucumbers
High-fiber pulses, lentils, and sprouted beans
Healthy fats: extra virgin olive oil, walnuts, chia seeds
Lean proteins: chicken breast, fish, tofu, paneer
avoid: Sugary sodas, packaged juices, and sweetened teas/coffees
Refined flour pastries, white bread, and sweets
Deep-fried snacks and trans-fat loaded processed foods
Excessive tropical sweet fruits (mangoes, chiku) in uncontrolled states

lifestyle_tips: Log fasting and 2-hour post-meal blood sugar levels in a glucometer logbook.
Inspect your feet daily for small cuts, blisters, or calluses to prevent diabetic foot ulcers.
Schedule annual dilated eye exams and kidney microalbuminuria tests.
emergency_red_flags: Blood glucose dropping below 70 mg/dL with tremors, sweating, confusion (Hypoglycemia - consume fast sugar immediately!)
Fruity breath odor, rapid breathing, vomiting, confusion (Diabetic Ketoacidosis - DKA)
Extremely high blood sugar (>400 mg/dL) with drowsiness or disorientation
Non-healing foot ulcer showing redness, blackening, or discharge

name: Pneumonia
overview: An infection that inflames the air sacs (alveoli) in one or both lungs, which may fill with fluid or purulent pus.
detailed_explanation: Pneumonia can be bacterial (Streptococcus pneumoniae), viral (influenza, SARS-CoV-2), or fungal. When microbes overcome host defense mechanisms, inflammatory exudate floods the alveoli, severely impairing alveolar gas exchange and leading to hypoxemia.
causes_and_triggers: Infection with Streptococcus pneumoniae, Mycoplasma, or respiratory viruses
Aspiration of food or fluids into respiratory passages
Recent preceding viral illness like severe influenza
Compromised immunity or chronic smoking

medicines.name: Amoxicillin-Clavulanate or Azithromycin
medicines.purpose: Antibacterial therapy targeting causative respiratory pathogens in bacterial pneumonia
medicines.instructions: As specifically prescribed by your doctor. Complete the entire 5 to 7 day course without skipping.
medicines.precautions: Antibiotics are ineffective against viral pneumonia. Never self-prescribe antibiotics.

medicines.name: Acetaminophen
medicines.purpose: Control high fever and relieve pleuritic chest discomfort
medicines.instructions: 500-650 mg every 6 hours as needed.
medicines.precautions: Ensure adequate fluid intake.

medicines.name: Guaifenesin
medicines.purpose: Expectorant to thin thick alveolar mucus secretions
medicines.instructions: 200-400 mg every 4 hours with full glasses of water.
medicines.precautions: Drink plenty of fluids for the expectorant to work effectively.

remedies.name: Chest Physical Therapy & Postural Drainage
remedies.description: Gentle percussion on the back while lying in specific positions guided by a caregiver.
remedies.benefit: Loosens thick, sticky lung secretions so they can be coughed out.

remedies.name: Incentive Spirometer Exercises
remedies.description: Inhale slowly and deeply through an incentive spirometer device 10 times every waking hour.
remedies.benefit: Re-expands collapsed alveoli (prevents atelectasis) and improves oxygen saturation.

remedies.name: Warm Fluid Ingestion
remedies.description: Drink warm lemon water, herbal teas, and hot clear broths frequently.
remedies.benefit: Prevents dehydration caused by high fever and thins respiratory tract secretions.

recommended: High-calorie nutrient-dense soups and stews
Easily digestible proteins: soft eggs, boiled chicken, lentils
Warm turmeric golden milk
Hydrating fresh coconut water and warm water
avoid: Cold dairy if it makes mucus feel thicker
Fried, oily, and heavy hard-to-chew foods
Carbonated beverages and sugary sodas

lifestyle_tips: Maintain strict bed rest until cleared by your physician.
Do not smoke or expose yourself to wood smoke or chemical fumes.
Stay up-to-date with annual pneumococcal and influenza vaccinations.
diagnostic_tests: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with high WBC count
emergency_red_flags: Oxygen saturation falling below 92%
Severe stabbing chest pain that stops you from inhaling
Coughing up rust-colored or frank red blood
Cyanosis (bluish tint around lips and fingertips) or confusion in elderly individuals

name: Urinary Tract Infection (UTI / Cystitis)
overview: An infection in any part of the urinary system, most commonly the bladder (cystitis) and urethra.
detailed_explanation: UTIs are predominantly caused by uropathogenic Escherichia coli (E. coli) originating from the gastrointestinal flora ascending through the urethra into the bladder. Women are at higher risk due to shorter urethral length. Untreated lower UTIs can ascend to kidneys (pyelonephritis).
causes_and_triggers: Bacterial contamination (E. coli ascending from bowel)
Delayed urination / holding urine for extended periods
Inadequate daily fluid intake
Sexual intercourse or use of diaphragms and spermicides

medicines.name: Nitrofurantoin or Fosfomycin
medicines.purpose: First-line urinary antibiotic targeting common uropathogens
medicines.instructions: Nitrofurantoin 100 mg twice daily for 5 days with food, or Fosfomycin 3g single sachet dose.
medicines.precautions: Requires physician prescription. Do not stop early even if burning subsides.

medicines.name: Phenazopyridine
medicines.purpose: Urinary tract local analgesic to relieve intense dysuria and spasms
medicines.instructions: 100-200 mg three times daily after meals for maximum 2 days.
medicines.precautions: Harmlessly discolors urine and contact lenses to bright reddish-orange.

medicines.name: Disodium Hydrogen Citrate (Urinary Alkalinizer)
medicines.purpose: Alkalinizes acidic urine to immediately alleviate burning sensation
medicines.instructions: Mix 2 teaspoons in a full glass of water and drink 2-3 times daily.
medicines.precautions: Use caution in patients with sodium restrictions or hypertension.

remedies.name: High-Volume Water Ingestion
remedies.description: Drink at least 2.5 to 3.5 liters of pure water throughout the day.
remedies.benefit: Mechanically flushes bacteria out of the urinary tract lumen before they adhere to epithelial walls.

remedies.name: Unsweetened Pure Cranberry Juice / D-Mannose
remedies.description: Consume 100% pure unsweetened cranberry juice or 2g D-Mannose powder daily.
remedies.benefit: Proanthocyanidins prevent bacterial fimbriae from adhering to the urothelial lining.

remedies.name: Warm Heating Pad on Lower Abdomen
remedies.description: Apply a hot water bottle or electric heating pad to your pubic area for 15 minutes.
remedies.benefit: Relieves bladder spasms and localized pelvic discomfort.

recommended: Abundant clean water
Probiotic foods (plain yogurt, kefir) to restore healthy flora
High-antioxidant blueberries and cranberries
Cucumbers and watermelon for natural mild diuresis
avoid: Caffeine (coffee, strong teas), which irritates the bladder wall
Alcohol and carbonated soda drinks
Spicy curries and artificial sweeteners
Citrus fruit juices if they aggravate burning

lifestyle_tips: Wipe strictly from front to back after using the toilet to avoid transferring bacteria.
Urinate promptly after sexual intercourse to flush out any bacteria.
Avoid holding your urine; empty your bladder as soon as you feel the urge.
diagnostic_tests: Urinalysis (Urine Routine & Microscopy for leukocytes, nitrites)
Urine Culture and Antibiotic Sensitivity (Urine C/S)
emergency_red_flags: High fever with severe shaking chills
Severe pain in the flank or lower back (Kidney region)
Nausea and recurrent vomiting alongside urinary symptoms
Frank gross blood (hematuria) in urine

name: Dengue Fever
overview: A mosquito-borne viral infection causing high fever, severe retro-orbital eye pain, joint pain, and potential thrombocytopenia.
detailed_explanation: Dengue virus (DENV-1 to DENV-4) is transmitted by daytime-biting female Aedes aegypti mosquitoes. It is notorious as 'breakbone fever' due to excruciating bone and muscle pain. Its critical danger phase starts around day 3-7 when fever subsides, risking plasma leakage, internal hemorrhage, and sharp platelet drop.
causes_and_triggers: Bite of an infected Aedes aegypti or Aedes albopictus mosquito
Stagnant water containers around houses (flower pots, buckets, coolers)
Warm tropical and subtropical rainy seasons

medicines.name: Paracetamol (Acetaminophen)
medicines.purpose: Only approved antipyretic to control fever and pain in suspected dengue
medicines.instructions: 500-650 mg every 6 hours as needed. Strict adherence to maximum dose limits.
medicines.precautions: CRITICAL: NEVER take Aspirin, Ibuprofen, Diclofenac, or any NSAIDs! They inhibit platelets and can trigger catastrophic internal bleeding.

medicines.name: Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS)
medicines.purpose: Maintains intravascular volume and prevents hypovolemic shock from capillary leakage
medicines.instructions: Sip ORS and fluids regularly throughout waking hours.
medicines.precautions: Maintain accurate fluid intake/output balance.

remedies.name: Papaya Leaf Extract
remedies.description: Crush 2-3 fresh thoroughly washed young papaya leaves, extract 10-15 ml juice, consume twice daily.
remedies.benefit: Contains carpaine and flavonoids shown in clinical studies to support platelet count recovery.

remedies.name: Coconut Water & Fresh Pomegranate Juice
remedies.description: Drink fresh green tender coconut water and pomegranate juice 3 times daily.
remedies.benefit: Restores vital electrolytes and supplies easily absorbable iron and hydration.

remedies.name: Strict Mosquito Bed Net Usage
remedies.description: Rest under an insecticide-treated mosquito bed net even during the daytime.
remedies.benefit: Prevents other mosquitoes from biting you and spreading the virus to family members.

recommended: Freshly prepared soups and porridges (khichdi, congee)
Kiwi, pomegranate, and dragon fruit for vitamin C and minerals
Electrolyte fluids: ORS, lemon water with salt, coconut water
Boiled vegetables and mashed bananas
avoid: Dark colored or red foods (beetroot, red sodas) that could confuse stool color in case of GI bleed
Hard, abrasive, or crispy snacks that could scratch mouth lining
Spicy, oily, and heavy fried foods

lifestyle_tips: Monitor platelet counts with daily Complete Blood Count (CBC) tests during days 3 to 7.
Eliminate all standing water sources in coolers, tire heaps, and flower pots within 100 meters of home.
Wear long-sleeved light-colored clothing and apply DEET/Picaridin mosquito repellent.
diagnostic_tests: Dengue NS1 Antigen ELISA (best during first 5 days)
Daily CBC to track Platelet count and Hematocrit (HCT)
emergency_red_flags: Severe persistent abdominal pain or persistent vomiting
Bleeding from gums, nose, or blood in vomit/stool (Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever)
Platelets dropping below 20,000 / μL or hematocrit rising rapidly
Cold, clammy extremities, rapid weak pulse, lethargy (Dengue Shock Syndrome - CALL EMERGENCY IMMEDIATELY)

name: Acute Appendicitis
overview: Acute inflammation of the vermiform appendix, presenting a medical emergency requiring rapid intervention.
detailed_explanation: Acute appendicitis occurs when the lumen of the appendix becomes obstructed by a fecalith (hardened stool), lymphoid hyperplasia, or foreign body. Luminal bacteria proliferate rapidly, intraluminal pressure mounts, venous thrombosis occurs, and ischemia develops. Without swift surgical excision, perforation occurs within 24-72 hours, resulting in peritonitis and life-threatening sepsis.
causes_and_triggers: Obstruction of the appendix opening by a fecalith
Enlarged lymphoid follicles following a gastrointestinal infection
Intestinal parasites or rare benign tumors

medicines.name: Intravenous Antibiotics & Analgesics (Hospital Administration)
medicines.purpose: Broad-spectrum coverage prior to laparoscopic appendectomy surgery
medicines.instructions: Administered exclusively in an emergency hospital setting by medical staff.
medicines.precautions: CRITICAL: DO NOT take painkiller medications, laxatives, or enemas at home! Painkillers can mask the worsening of symptoms, and laxatives can cause the inflamed appendix to rupture immediately!

remedies.name: NO Home Remedies - Emergency Medical Transport
remedies.description: Do NOT apply heating pads to the abdomen (heat accelerates perforation). Do NOT eat or drink anything (keep stomach empty for emergency surgery).
remedies.benefit: Immediate surgical consultation prevents peritonitis and abdominal sepsis.

recommended: Strictly NPO (Nothing by mouth) - do not eat or drink anything until evaluated by an emergency surgeon.
avoid: All foods, liquids, water, and oral pills until hospital clearance.

lifestyle_tips: Lie completely still with knees bent toward chest to lessen abdominal wall tension while awaiting emergency transport.
Go straight to the nearest Emergency Department (ER).
emergency_red_flags: Sudden temporary relief of pain followed by widespread agonizing abdominal rigidity (indicates appendix rupture!)
High fever, shaking chills, and rapid heart rate
Inability to walk upright due to severe sharp right pelvic pain
Extreme abdominal rigidity (board-like belly)

name: Eczema (Atopic Dermatitis)
overview: A chronic inflammatory skin condition characterized by dry, itchy, red, and irritated patches of skin.
detailed_explanation: Atopic dermatitis involves a genetic dysfunction of the skin barrier (often linked to filaggrin gene mutations) combined with an overactive cutaneous immune response. The damaged stratum corneum permits excessive trans-epidermal water loss and allows allergens and irritants to penetrate, triggering persistent pruritus and the 'itch-scratch' vicious cycle.
causes_and_triggers: Defective epidermal skin barrier proteins
Harsh chemical soaps, detergents, and synthetic fabrics (wool, polyester)
Dry, low-humidity winter weather or hot baths
Food allergens, dust mites, pet dander, and psychological stress

medicines.name: Hydrocortisone 1% Cream or Betamethasone
medicines.purpose: Topical corticosteroid to rapidly calm acute flare-up redness and dermal inflammation
medicines.instructions: Apply a thin layer strictly to affected areas once or twice daily for up to 7-10 days.
medicines.precautions: Avoid using potent topical steroids on the face, groin, or eyelids without dermatologist supervision to prevent skin thinning (atrophy).

medicines.name: Tacrolimus / Pimecrolimus Ointment
medicines.purpose: Non-steroidal topical calcineurin inhibitor for sensitive facial and flexural areas
medicines.instructions: Apply twice daily as prescribed.
medicines.precautions: May cause a mild burning or warm sensation for the first few days.

medicines.name: Diphenhydramine or Cetirizine
medicines.purpose: Oral antihistamine to suppress nighttime itching and enable restful sleep
medicines.instructions: Take 1 dose 30-60 minutes before bedtime.
medicines.precautions: First-generation antihistamines (diphenhydramine) cause sedation.

remedies.name: The 'Soak and Seal' Moisturizing Method
remedies.description: Take a 5-10 minute lukewarm shower, gently pat skin partially dry, and slather on a thick ceramide-rich ointment or cream within 3 minutes.
remedies.benefit: Locks moisture directly into the stratum corneum before it evaporates.

remedies.name: Colloidal Oatmeal Baths
remedies.description: Add 1 cup of finely ground colloidal oatmeal to lukewarm bathwater and soak for 15 minutes.
remedies.benefit: Avenanthramides in oatmeal exert potent anti-inflammatory and antipruritic soothing effects.

remedies.name: Virgin Cold-Pressed Coconut Oil
remedies.description: Gently massage pure virgin coconut oil onto damp dry patches twice daily.
remedies.benefit: Provides natural lauric acid with antimicrobial properties against Staphylococcus aureus colonisation.

recommended: Anti-inflammatory foods rich in Omega-3 (wild salmon, flaxseeds, chia seeds)
Quercetin-rich foods (apples, blueberries, kale)
Probiotics (kefir, yogurt) to support gut-skin immune axis
Ample water intake
avoid: Identified food triggers (common: cow's milk, eggs, gluten, soy in sensitive individuals)
Refined sugars and processed junk food
Excessive spicy seasonings that promote skin flushing

lifestyle_tips: Wear loose-fitting, soft 100% cotton clothing; avoid coarse wool and rough synthetics.
Keep fingernails trimmed short and filed smooth to minimize skin trauma during subconscious sleep scratching.
Use fragrance-free, hypoallergenic liquid laundry detergents and mild soap-free body cleansers.
diagnostic_tests: Skin biopsy (rare, only to exclude cutaneous lymphoma or psoriasis)
emergency_red_flags: Skin develops honey-colored crusts, oozing yellow pus, or red streaks (Secondary Bacterial Impetigo)
Sudden outbreak of painful blisters accompanied by fever (Eczema Herpeticum - EMERGENCY)
Severe widespread erythroderma covering over 90% of body surface area

name: Allergic Rhinitis (Hay Fever)
overview: An allergic immune response in the nasal passages triggered by airborne environmental allergens.
detailed_explanation: Allergic rhinitis occurs when an individual's IgE antibodies mistakenly identify harmless airborne particles (pollen, dust mites, molds) as dangerous invaders. Cross-linking of IgE on mast cells triggers massive histamine, leukotriene, and prostaglandin degranulation, causing watery rhinorrhea, itching, and sneezing fits.
causes_and_triggers: Seasonal tree, grass, and weed pollens
Indoor perennial allergens: dust mites, cockroach droppings, cat/dog saliva and dander
Airborne mold spores in damp basements or bathrooms

medicines.name: Fluticasone Propionate Nasal Spray
medicines.purpose: First-line intranasal corticosteroid that blocks multiple inflammatory cytokines
medicines.instructions: 1-2 sprays in each nostril once daily. Point nozzle slightly outward away from nasal septum.
medicines.precautions: Takes 2-4 days of daily use for full therapeutic efficacy; not an instant fix.

medicines.name: Fexofenadine / Levocetirizine
medicines.purpose: Non-drowsy second-generation oral antihistamine to stop itching and sneezing
medicines.instructions: Fexofenadine 120-180 mg once daily with a glass of water.
medicines.precautions: Do not take fexofenadine with grapefruit or apple juice as it decreases absorption.

medicines.name: Olopatadine Eye Drops
medicines.purpose: Dual-action antihistamine and mast cell stabilizer for red, itchy allergic eyes
medicines.instructions: 1 drop in each affected eye once or twice daily.
medicines.precautions: Remove contact lenses prior to application.

remedies.name: Neti Pot Nasal Saline Irrigation
remedies.description: Rinse each nasal passage with distilled or boiled-and-cooled isotonic saline using a Neti pot.
remedies.benefit: Physically flushes trapped pollen grains, particulate allergens, and inflammatory mucus out of the nasal cavity.

remedies.name: HEPA Air Filtration & Bedroom Sanctuary
remedies.description: Run a true HEPA air filter in the bedroom 24/7 with closed windows.
remedies.benefit: Reduces airborne allergen concentration by up to 99% during sleep.

remedies.name: Post-Outdoors Shower & Wardrobe Change
remedies.description: Shower immediately and wash hair after returning home during high pollen count days.
remedies.benefit: Prevents transfer of outdoor pollens onto pillows, bedding, and furniture.

recommended: Quercetin-rich foods (red onions, capers, berries) acting as natural mast-cell stabilizers
Turmeric and ginger warm teas
Vitamin C rich citrus, kiwis, and bell peppers
Omega-3 rich foods
avoid: Cross-reactive fruits causing Oral Allergy Syndrome (e.g. raw apples/peaches during birch pollen season)
Excessive alcohol which triggers histamine release and nasal vasodilation

lifestyle_tips: Check daily pollen forecasts; keep house and car windows closed during peak pollen hours (5 AM - 10 AM).
Wear wraparound sunglasses outdoors to shield conjunctiva from pollen contact.
Wash bed sheets and pillowcases weekly in hot water (at least 130°F / 54°C) to kill dust mites.
emergency_red_flags: Sudden swelling of the tongue, lips, throat or airway (Anaphylaxis - EMERGENCY)
Audible wheezing or severe difficulty drawing breath
Development of severe facial sinus pain with high fever (acute secondary bacterial sinusitis)

name: Typhoid Fever (Enteric Fever)
overview: A systemic bacterial infection caused by Salmonella Typhi, characterized by prolonged high 'step-ladder' fever and abdominal symptoms.
detailed_explanation: Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi colonizes the human intestinal mucosa, penetrates Peyer's patches, and spreads via the reticuloendothelial system into bloodstream, liver, spleen, and gallbladder. Without antibiotic therapy, it causes severe complications such as intestinal perforation, encephalitis, and septic shock.
causes_and_triggers: Ingestion of food or water contaminated with feces or urine of infected individuals or chronic carriers
Street food prepared with untreated water or unhygienic ice
Lack of clean hand hygiene before dining

medicines.name: Ceftriaxone or Azithromycin
medicines.purpose: Definitive antibiotic therapy to eradicate systemic Salmonella Typhi bacteria
medicines.instructions: Ceftriaxone IV in hospital or oral Azithromycin 500-1000mg daily for 7-14 days as directed by doctor.
medicines.precautions: Must complete the full antibiotic course even after fever breaks to prevent chronic carrier state.

medicines.name: Paracetamol
medicines.purpose: Antipyretic to manage high fever
medicines.instructions: 650 mg every 6 hours as needed for high temperature.
medicines.precautions: Avoid NSAIDs (Ibuprofen) due to risk of gastrointestinal irritation and bleeding.

remedies.name: Boiled & Filtered Water Only
remedies.description: Boil all drinking water vigorously for at least 1 minute before cooling and drinking.
remedies.benefit: Destroys water-borne pathogens and prevents re-infection.

remedies.name: Cold Water Forehead Compresses
remedies.description: Place cool damp cloth compresses on the forehead, neck, and wrists during high-temperature surges.
remedies.benefit: Safely reduces core thermal stress during the prolonged step-ladder fever stages.

remedies.name: Continuous Oral Hydration Therapy
remedies.description: Drink 3 liters of fluid daily: ORS, barley water, thin strained rice gruel, and coconut water.
remedies.benefit: Combats severe dehydration and supports vital renal excretion.

recommended: High-calorie soft bland diet: khichdi, thin dal, mashed boiled potatoes
Custard, soft curd (yogurt), and fruit juices without pulp
Ripe bananas, applesauce, and white bread
Plenty of light broths
avoid: High-fiber coarse vegetables and raw salads that irritate inflamed Peyer's patches
Spicy curries, fried snacks, and strong seasonings
Gas-forming foods: cabbage, cauliflower, beans, carbonated drinks

lifestyle_tips: Strict isolation and hand hygiene with antibacterial soap after every restroom visit.
Ensure complete physical bed rest for at least 2 full weeks.
Get the Typhoid conjugate vaccine (TCV) before traveling to endemic areas.
emergency_red_flags: Sudden severe agonizing abdominal pain and board-like rigidity (Intestinal Perforation)
Vomiting blood or dark black tarry stools (Severe GI hemorrhage)
Altered mental status, stupor, delirium ('Typhoid state')
Persistent hypothermia or rapid drop in blood pressure

name: Osteoarthritis
overview: A degenerative joint disease where the protective cartilage that cushions the ends of bones wears down over time.
detailed_explanation: Osteoarthritis is a whole-joint disorder involving cartilage degradation, subchondral bone remodeling, osteophyte (bone spur) formation, and synovial inflammation. Most commonly affecting weight-bearing joints (knees, hips, lumbar spine) and hands, it results in pain on activity and morning stiffness lasting less than 30 minutes.
causes_and_triggers: Age-related natural cartilage wear and tear
Joint overuse, repetitive occupational stress, or previous traumatic joint injury
Obesity increasing mechanical loads on knee and hip joints
Genetics and joint misalignment

medicines.name: Topical Diclofenac Gel (Voltaren)
medicines.purpose: Local NSAID that penetrates joint capsules to relieve pain without systemic gastric side effects
medicines.instructions: Apply 2-4 grams to affected joint 3 to 4 times daily and massage gently.
medicines.precautions: Wash hands after applying; do not apply to broken or cut skin.

medicines.name: Acetaminophen (Paracetamol)
medicines.purpose: Mild analgesic for baseline mild-to-moderate joint ache
medicines.instructions: 650-1000 mg every 6-8 hours with food.
medicines.precautions: Do not exceed recommended daily threshold.

medicines.name: Celecoxib (COX-2 Inhibitor)
medicines.purpose: Targeted oral anti-inflammatory with reduced gastric ulcer risk
medicines.instructions: 100-200 mg orally once daily with food.
medicines.precautions: Caution in patients with underlying cardiovascular risks.

remedies.name: Low-Impact Aerobic Exercise (Swimming / Water Aerobics)
remedies.description: Engage in 30 minutes of swimming or stationary recumbent biking 3 times weekly.
remedies.benefit: Strengthens quadriceps and stabilizing muscles without subjecting knee joints to gravitational impact.

remedies.name: Alternating Warm and Cold Therapy
remedies.description: Apply a warm compress before exercise to loosen stiff joints; apply cold ice pack for 15 minutes after activity.
remedies.benefit: Heat improves synovial fluid circulation; cold diminishes post-activity inflammatory flare-ups.

remedies.name: Knee Bracing and Supportive Orthotics
remedies.description: Use an unloader knee brace or cushioned arch-support shoe inserts.
remedies.benefit: Redistributes biomechanical weight loads away from damaged cartilage compartments.

recommended: Fatty cold-water fish rich in Omega-3 (salmon, mackerel, sardines)
Turmeric with black pepper (curcumin has demonstrated anti-inflammatory joint benefits)
Glucosamine and chondroitin-rich bone broths
Berries and citrus fruits
avoid: Refined sugars and corn syrup that promote systemic cytokine inflammation
Processed red meats and high-saturated fats
Excessive salt which causes fluid retention

lifestyle_tips: Target a 5-10% body weight reduction: every 1 pound of weight lost takes 4 pounds of pressure off your knees!
Avoid deep squats, heavy lunges, or prolonged sitting on low stools.
Use a cane or walking stick held in the hand opposite the painful joint to offload up to 30% of force.
diagnostic_tests: Weight-bearing Joint X-Rays (showing joint space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis, osteophytes)
emergency_red_flags: Joint suddenly becomes hot, brightly red, and excruciatingly swollen (ruling out Septic Arthritis)
Complete inability to bear any weight on the leg after minimal strain
Numbness or tingling shooting down the leg (Spinal nerve compression)

name: Kidney Stones (Nephrolithiasis)
overview: Hard mineral and salt deposits that form inside the kidneys and cause excruciating colicky flank pain when traveling down the ureter.
detailed_explanation: Kidney stones crystallize when urinary solute concentration exceeds solubility limits (super-saturation). The most common types are Calcium Oxalate (80%), Uric Acid, Struvite, and Cystine. When a stone dislodges and lodges in the narrow ureter, it causes proximal hydroureteronephrosis and intense paroxysmal renal colic.
causes_and_triggers: Chronic low fluid intake and chronic dehydration
Diets high in sodium, animal purines, or high-oxalate foods (spinach, nuts, chocolate)
Hypercalciuria, hyperparathyroidism, or gout
Genetic metabolic predisposition

medicines.name: Ketorolac / Ibuprofen (NSAIDs)
medicines.purpose: Primary analgesic that reduces ureteral smooth muscle inflammation and spasm
medicines.instructions: Administered under medical supervision for acute renal colic.
medicines.precautions: Ensure renal function is monitored; avoid in acute kidney injury.

medicines.name: Tamsulosin (Alpha-1 Blocker)
medicines.purpose: Relaxes the smooth muscles of the distal ureter to facilitate spontaneous stone passage
medicines.instructions: 0.4 mg orally once daily after the same meal each day.
medicines.precautions: May cause orthostatic dizziness or retrograde ejaculation.

medicines.name: Potassium Citrate
medicines.purpose: Alkalinizes urine to dissolve and prevent uric acid and calcium oxalate crystals
medicines.instructions: As prescribed based on 24-hour urine collection results.
medicines.precautions: Monitor serum potassium levels.

remedies.name: Aggressive Water Hydration (Water Flushes)
remedies.description: Drink 2.5 to 3 liters of water evenly throughout the day and night.
remedies.benefit: Creates strong urinary hydrostatic pressure to propel small stones (<5mm) down the ureter.

remedies.name: Fresh Lemon Water Daily
remedies.description: Squeeze the juice of two fresh lemons into a liter of drinking water.
remedies.benefit: Natural dietary citrate binds to urinary calcium, preventing crystal aggregation and growth.

remedies.name: Urine Straining & Collection
remedies.description: Urinate through a fine mesh stone strainer into a clean cup.
remedies.benefit: Captures passed stone fragments for laboratory composition analysis.

recommended: Plenty of pure water and lemon/lime water
Normal healthy dietary calcium (milk, yogurt) which binds oxalate in gut
Fresh fruits and vegetables rich in potassium and magnesium
avoid: Excessive animal protein (red meats, organ meats) which increases uric acid
High-oxalate foods: spinach, beets, rhubarb, almonds, chocolate
Excessive sodium and salty snacks that force calcium into urine

lifestyle_tips: Never wait until you are thirsty to drink water; urine should always look pale straw or crystal clear.
Stay active; gentle walking can assist gravitational descent of stones through the ureters.
diagnostic_tests: Non-Contrast Helical Abdominal CT Scan (Gold Standard)
emergency_red_flags: Fever and shaking chills accompanying flank pain (Obstructed infected kidney - UROLOGICAL EMERGENCY)
Complete anuria (inability to pass any urine for hours)
Intractable vomiting preventing any fluid retention
Unbearable pain unresponsive to heavy analgesics

name: Peptic Ulcer Disease
overview: Sores or breaks that develop on the inside lining of your stomach (gastric ulcer) or the upper portion of your small intestine (duodenal ulcer).
detailed_explanation: Peptic ulcers arise from an imbalance between aggressive digestive forces (gastric acid, pepsin) and protective mucosal defense mechanisms (mucus layer, bicarbonate, prostaglandins). The vast majority are triggered by Helicobacter pylori bacterial infection or habitual use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs).
causes_and_triggers: Infection with Helicobacter pylori bacteria
Frequent, regular use of NSAIDs (Ibuprofen, Naproxen, Aspirin, Diclofenac)
Cigarette smoking and excessive alcohol consumption
Severe physiological stress

medicines.name: H. Pylori Eradication Triple/Quadruple Therapy (Clarithromycin + Amoxicillin + PPI)
medicines.purpose: Eradicates underlying bacterial infection and stops acid production to heal ulcer crater
medicines.instructions: Strict 14-day protocol prescribed by gastroenterologist.
medicines.precautions: Take every single dose exactly on time to prevent bacterial antibiotic resistance.

medicines.name: Pantoprazole / Esomeprazole
medicines.purpose: Suppresses gastric acid pumps to allow mucosal regeneration
medicines.instructions: 40 mg once daily 30 minutes before breakfast for 4-8 weeks.
medicines.precautions: Do not abruptly stop without consulting your doctor.

medicines.name: Sucralfate Suspension
medicines.purpose: Forms a protective chemical barrier over the ulcer crater protecting it from acid and pepsin
medicines.instructions: 1 gram suspension 4 times daily on an empty stomach (1 hour before meals and at bedtime).
medicines.precautions: Space 2 hours apart from other medications as it binds them.

remedies.name: Cabbage Juice Protocol
remedies.description: Drink 100-150 ml of freshly extracted raw green cabbage juice daily.
remedies.benefit: Rich in S-methylmethionine (Vitamin U) and glutamine that accelerates gastric epithelial repair.

remedies.name: Deglycyrrhizinated Licorice (DGL)
remedies.description: Chew 1-2 DGL tablets 20 minutes before meals.
remedies.benefit: Stimulates natural stomach mucus production without raising blood pressure.

remedies.name: Probiotic Rich Foods (Kefir / Plain Curd)
remedies.description: Consume 1 bowl of fresh unsweetened yogurt or probiotic kefir daily.
remedies.benefit: Suppresses H. pylori colonization and reduces antibiotic-associated diarrhea.

recommended: Bland cooked oats, rice, and steamed sweet potatoes
Lean chicken, white fish, and soft boiled eggs
Apples, pears, and bananas
Non-acidic vegetable broths and herbal teas
avoid: NSAIDs (Aspirin, Ibuprofen, Diclofenac) - STRICTLY AVOID
Black pepper, red chili powder, and harsh spices
Coffee, caffeinated drinks, and alcohol
Fried greasy meats and sour tomato sauces

lifestyle_tips: Eat small, evenly spaced meals throughout the day so your stomach is never completely empty for prolonged hours.
Stop smoking immediately, as nicotine significantly impairs stomach blood flow and mucosal healing.
Manage stress levels with relaxation techniques.
diagnostic_tests: Urea Breath Test (UBT) for H. pylori
Stool Antigen Test for H. pylori
emergency_red_flags: Vomiting bright red blood or dark digested blood that looks like coffee grounds (Hematemesis)
Passing foul-smelling, jet-black, sticky tarry stools (Melena)
Sudden, sharp, agonizing abdominal pain that spreads rapidly across the whole stomach (Ulcer Perforation)
Feeling faint, dizzy, or passing out (Hypovolemic shock from internal hemorrhage)

name: Acute & Chronic Sinusitis (Rhinosinusitis)
overview: Inflammation or swelling of the tissue lining the paranasal sinuses, blocking mucus drainage and leading to facial pressure.
detailed_explanation: Paranasal sinuses are air-filled spaces in the facial bones. When the ostia (drainage pathways) become occluded by mucosal edema from a cold or allergies, mucus accumulates. Bacteria (Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae) or viruses proliferate in the trapped secretions, causing pressure over the cheeks, forehead, or between the eyes.
causes_and_triggers: Prolonged viral upper respiratory infection (common cold)
Allergic rhinitis causing mucosal swelling
Deviated nasal septum or nasal polyps blocking ostia
Swimming in chlorinated or polluted water

medicines.name: Mometasone or Fluticasone Nasal Spray
medicines.purpose: Corticosteroid spray to shrink swollen sinus ostial mucosa and promote natural drainage
medicines.instructions: 2 sprays in each nostril once daily.
medicines.precautions: Do not blow nose aggressively immediately after spraying.

medicines.name: Amoxicillin-Clavulanate (Augmentin)
medicines.purpose: Antibiotic reserved strictly for bacterial sinusitis (symptoms lasting >10 days without improvement or 'double sickening')
medicines.instructions: Taken as prescribed for 7-10 days.
medicines.precautions: Take with meals to prevent gastrointestinal upset.

medicines.name: Acetaminophen or Ibuprofen
medicines.purpose: Relieves throbbing facial sinus pressure and forehead headache
medicines.instructions: As directed on package.
medicines.precautions: Avoid overuse.

remedies.name: Hypertonic Saline Nasal Irrigation
remedies.description: Irrigate nasal passages with warm hypertonic saline 2-3 times daily using a sinus rinse squeeze bottle.
remedies.benefit: Physically thins and draws out stagnant tenacious mucopurulent secretions.

remedies.name: Warm Facial Compress
remedies.description: Place a warm, moist towel across your forehead, cheeks, and eyes for 10 minutes 3 times a day.
remedies.benefit: Increases local circulation, eases localized pain, and encourages sinus ostial opening.

remedies.name: Menthol / Eucalyptus Steam Inhalation
remedies.description: Inhale steam over a basin of hot water with 2 drops of eucalyptus essential oil.
remedies.benefit: Promotes ciliary beat frequency and eases airway congestion.

recommended: Warm spicy soups with garlic, ginger, and turmeric (natural decongestants)
Pineapple (contains bromelain, an enzyme that reduces sinus swelling)
Hot herbal teas (peppermint, chamomile)
Copious amounts of warm water
avoid: Chilled and iced drinks
Excessive dairy products if they make mucus feel unpleasantly viscous
Alcohol which dehydrates and swells nasal membranes

lifestyle_tips: Sleep with your head elevated on two pillows to facilitate nighttime sinus drainage.
Use a cool-mist room humidifier next to your bed.
Avoid rapid air pressure changes (flying or scuba diving) during acute flare-ups.
diagnostic_tests: Sinus aspirate culture (in refractory chronic cases)
emergency_red_flags: Swelling, redness, or drooping around one or both eyes (Orbital Cellulitis)
Double vision or sudden reduction in visual acuity
Severe stiff neck, high fever, and extreme lethargy (Meningitis complication)
Forehead soft-tissue swelling (Pott's puffy tumor)

name: Malaria
overview: A life-threatening disease caused by Plasmodium parasites transmitted to people through the bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.
detailed_explanation: Plasmodium falciparum, vivax, ovale, and malariae invade hepatocyte liver cells before entering erythrocytes (red blood cells). The synchronized cyclical rupture of infected red blood cells releases merozoites, hemozoin, and pyrogens into the bloodstream, triggering classic paroxysmal cycles of violent shivering chills (cold stage), blazing fever (hot stage), and profuse sweating (sweating stage).
causes_and_triggers: Bite of an infective female Anopheles mosquito (bites predominantly between dusk and dawn)
Plasmodium falciparum infection (most lethal form)
Travel to tropical endemic regions without prophylaxis

medicines.name: Artemether-Lumefantrine (Artemisinin Combination Therapy - ACT)
medicines.purpose: First-line rapid-acting parasiticidal agent against Plasmodium blood stages
medicines.instructions: 6-dose regimen over 3 days as strictly prescribed by physician.
medicines.precautions: Take with high-fat meals or milk to guarantee optimal lumefantrine intestinal absorption.

medicines.name: Primaquine
medicines.purpose: Eliminates dormant liver hypnozoites in Plasmodium vivax and ovale to prevent future relapses
medicines.instructions: Daily for 14 days under physician orders.
medicines.precautions: Mandatory G6PD deficiency test before administration to prevent severe hemolytic anemia.

medicines.name: Paracetamol
medicines.purpose: Reduces high fever during paroxysms
medicines.instructions: 500-650 mg every 6 hours.
medicines.precautions: Keep hydrated; avoid aspirin.

remedies.name: Lukewarm Sponge Baths During Hot Stage
remedies.description: Wipe arms, legs, and forehead with lukewarm water towels when body temperature peaks.
remedies.benefit: Aids evaporative heat loss without provoking shivering.

remedies.name: Warm Blanketing During Cold Rigor Stage
remedies.description: Wrap in multiple dry warm blankets during the shivering stage; remove them once the hot fever stage sets in.
remedies.benefit: Provides comfort and reduces metabolic shivering exhaustion.

remedies.name: Electrolyte Fluid Replacement
remedies.description: Drink ORS and coconut water continuously to replace massive fluid loss from profuse drenching sweats.
remedies.benefit: Prevents severe hypovolemic dehydration and electrolyte imbalances.

recommended: High-energy easily digestible foods: boiled rice, porridge, mashed vegetables
Fresh citrus fruits (oranges, limes) rich in Vitamin C
Tender coconut water, clear chicken or vegetable soups
Steamed apples and bananas
avoid: Heavy, oily, deep-fried foods that exacerbate nausea
Spicy seasonings that irritate the gastrointestinal tract
Cold iced sodas and unpasteurized juices

lifestyle_tips: Sleep strictly under long-lasting insecticide-treated mosquito nets (LLINs).
Apply DEET or Icaridin insect repellent on exposed skin from sunset until sunrise.
Take prescribed chemoprophylaxis tablets (Doxycycline or Atovaquone-Proguanil) before and during travel to endemic zones.
diagnostic_tests: Peripheral Blood Smear (Thick and Thin smear microscopy with Giemsa stain)
Malaria Rapid Diagnostic Test (RDT for Pf-HRP2 and Pan-pLDH)
Complete Blood Count (showing anemia and thrombocytopenia)
emergency_red_flags: Confusion, seizures, or coma (Cerebral Malaria - IMMEDIATE ICU EMERGENCY)
Severe respiratory distress or deep acidotic breathing (ARDS)
Passing very dark black or brown urine (Blackwater Fever - acute hemoglobinuria)
Severe jaundice with yellow eyes and skin

name: Hypothyroidism (Underactive Thyroid)
overview: A condition in which the thyroid gland produces insufficient thyroid hormones, slowing down the body's overall metabolism.
detailed_explanation: Hypothyroidism is most commonly caused by Hashimoto's thyroiditis (an autoimmune destruction of the thyroid gland) or iodine deficiency. As free thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3) levels decline, the pituitary releases higher Thyroid Stimulating Hormone (TSH). The systemic metabolic rate decelerates across cardiovascular, neurological, and metabolic systems.
causes_and_triggers: Hashimoto's Autoimmune Thyroiditis
Surgical thyroidectomy or radioactive iodine therapy
Dietary iodine deficiency or excessive lithium/amiodarone medication
Pituitary gland disorders

medicines.name: Levothyroxine Sodium (Synthetic T4)
medicines.purpose: Bioidentical daily replacement of missing thyroid hormone to normalize basal metabolic rate
medicines.instructions: Take once daily in the morning on an empty stomach with a full glass of water, at least 30-60 minutes before breakfast.
medicines.precautions: Do not take iron, calcium, or antacid supplements within 4 hours of Levothyroxine as they prevent absorption.

remedies.name: Iodized Salt & Selenium Nutrition
remedies.description: Ensure use of standard iodized table salt and eat 2 Brazil nuts daily (rich in selenium).
remedies.benefit: Selenium is an essential co-factor for deiodinase enzymes that convert T4 to active T3.

remedies.name: Moderate Strength Training & Walking
remedies.description: Engage in 20-30 minutes of resistance training or brisk walking 4 times weekly.
remedies.benefit: Stimulates lean muscle mass retention and counteracts sluggish basal metabolic rate.

remedies.name: Warm Hydrotherapy & Layered Dressing
remedies.description: Wear thermal insulating layers and take warm showers.
remedies.benefit: Mitigates uncomfortable shivering and poor peripheral vasomotor constriction.

recommended: Iodized salt, seafood, and saltwater fish (cod, tuna)
Brazil nuts, sunflower seeds, and eggs for selenium and zinc
High-fiber vegetables and beans to overcome slow bowel motility
Plenty of water to support hydration and skin barrier
avoid: Excessive raw goitrogenic cruciferous vegetables (raw cabbage, broccoli, kale in extreme amounts)
Soy products within 2 hours of taking thyroid medication
Excessive processed gluten in autoimmune Hashimoto's sufferers

lifestyle_tips: Test serum TSH and Free T4 levels every 6 to 12 weeks during dose titration, and annually thereafter.
Establish consistent morning medication routine without skipping doses.
Ensure 7-8 hours of sound sleep.
diagnostic_tests: Serum Thyroid Stimulating Hormone (TSH) - elevated in primary hypothyroidism
Anti-Thyroid Peroxidase Antibodies (Anti-TPO) to verify Hashimoto's
emergency_red_flags: Myxedema Coma: severe hypothermia, profound lethargy, bradycardia, confusion (Life-threatening emergency)
Marked swelling of the tongue and vocal cords causing airway restriction
Severe fluid retention around heart (Pericardial effusion)

name: Gout (Gouty Arthritis)
overview: A painful form of inflammatory arthritis caused by high levels of uric acid in the blood forming sharp urate crystals in joints.
detailed_explanation: When serum uric acid exceeds its saturation threshold (hyperuricemia, typically >6.8 mg/dL), monosodium urate (MSU) needle-shaped microcrystals precipitate within the synovial fluid and joint tissues. This activates the NLRP3 inflammasome, triggering neutrophil infiltration and agonizing inflammatory flares, most famously in the first metatarsophalangeal joint (the big toe, known as podagra).
causes_and_triggers: High dietary purine consumption: red meat, organ meats, shellfish, beer
High-fructose corn syrup beverages and dehydration
Impaired renal uric acid excretion
Certain medications (thiazide diuretics, low-dose aspirin)

medicines.name: Colchicine
medicines.purpose: Interrupts microtubule assembly, preventing neutrophil migration and phagocytosis of urate crystals
medicines.instructions: 1.2 mg at first sign of flare, followed by 0.6 mg one hour later. Prescribed by doctor.
medicines.precautions: Do not overdose; can cause severe diarrhea and abdominal cramps.

medicines.name: Indomethacin or Naproxen (NSAIDs)
medicines.purpose: Powerful anti-inflammatory to quell severe joint swelling and pain
medicines.instructions: Take with meals as prescribed.
medicines.precautions: Take with gastroprotective agent if prone to gastritis.

medicines.name: Allopurinol / Febuxostat (Xanthine Oxidase Inhibitors)
medicines.purpose: Long-term daily preventive medication that lowers serum uric acid synthesis
medicines.instructions: Daily dose titrated to achieve serum uric acid <6.0 mg/dL.
medicines.precautions: DO NOT start or adjust Allopurinol during an acute flare, as fluctuating uric acid levels worsen the flare!

remedies.name: Ice Pack Application
remedies.description: Apply crushed ice wrapped in a damp towel to the inflamed joint for 20 minutes, 3-4 times daily.
remedies.benefit: Numbs acute intense pain and suppresses local microvascular hyperemia.

remedies.name: Joint Elevation with Bed Cradle
remedies.description: Elevate your foot on pillows higher than your heart level and tent your bedsheets so they don't press on the toe.
remedies.benefit: Reduces inflammatory interstitial fluid pooling and prevents excruciating tactile contact.

remedies.name: Tart Cherry Juice Consumption
remedies.description: Drink 8 ounces (240 ml) of 100% tart cherry juice daily.
remedies.benefit: Contains anthocyanins that inhibit xanthine oxidase and help accelerate renal urate excretion.

recommended: Low-fat milk, yogurt, and cottage cheese (proteins that promote uric acid excretion)
Cherries, blueberries, strawberries, and citrus fruits
Coffee (demonstrated to lower uric acid levels in observational trials)
3-4 liters of water daily to flush urate
avoid: Beer and distilled spirits - ALCOHOL IS A MAJOR TRIGGER
Organ meats (liver, kidneys, sweetbreads) and game meats
Anchovies, sardines, mussels, scallops, and mackerel
High-fructose corn syrup sodas and candies

lifestyle_tips: Maintain exceptional hydration; drink a large glass of water right before bedtime and upon waking.
Avoid crash diets and severe starvation fasting, which temporarily elevate serum uric acid levels.
Wear wide, comfortable footwear with roomy toe boxes.
diagnostic_tests: Arthrocentesis & Synovial Fluid Polarized Microscopy (showing negatively birefringent needle-shaped crystals)
emergency_red_flags: Fever and chills accompanying a fiery red swollen joint (Must immediately exclude Septic Arthritis via joint tap)
Skin breakdown over a joint with chalky white drainage (Infected tophi)
Acute inability to pass urine or severe flank pain (Uric acid kidney stones)

name: Acute Bronchitis
overview: Inflammation of the lining of the bronchial tubes, which carry air to and from the lungs, usually caused by a viral infection.
detailed_explanation: Acute bronchitis is predominantly viral in etiology (>90% caused by influenza, parainfluenza, RSV, or coronavirus). The bronchial mucosal lining swells and hyper-secretes mucus, triggering a persistent, racking cough that lasts 2 to 3 weeks even after viral clearance.
causes_and_triggers: Recent viral upper respiratory infection (cold or flu spreading downward)
Inhaling environmental irritants, cigarette smoke, or chemical vapors
Gastroesophageal reflux disease micro-aspiration

medicines.name: Guaifenesin (Mucolytic Expectorant)
medicines.purpose: Thins and liquefies bronchial mucus to make coughing more productive and less fatiguing
medicines.instructions: 200-400 mg every 4 hours with a large glass of water.
medicines.precautions: Hydration is necessary for optimal expectorant efficacy.

medicines.name: Dextromethorphan (for Nighttime)
medicines.purpose: Calms spasms to permit restorative sleep when cough is severe and unproductive at night
medicines.instructions: 10-20 mg before sleep.
medicines.precautions: Do not suppress a productive daytime cough which serves to clear pathogens.

medicines.name: Albuterol Inhaler (if wheezing)
medicines.purpose: Relieves transient bronchospasm in patients with reactive airways
medicines.instructions: 2 puffs every 4-6 hours as prescribed.
medicines.precautions: May cause transient tachycardia or hand tremor.

remedies.name: Warm Honey & Thyme Tea
remedies.description: Steep 1 teaspoon of dried thyme in boiling water for 10 minutes, strain, add 2 teaspoons of honey.
remedies.benefit: Thyme contains thymol with natural antispasmodic bronchial relaxing properties.

remedies.name: Steam Vaporizer with Peppermint
remedies.description: Breathe warm humidified air in a steam tent for 15 minutes twice daily.
remedies.benefit: Moistens mucosal membranes and reduces tracheobronchial hypersensitivity.

recommended: Warm herbal broths with garlic and turmeric
Hot water with honey and lemon
Antioxidant-rich berries and oranges
avoid: Cold beverages and ice creams
Dairy products if they increase mucus sensation
Cigarette smoke and aerosol sprays

lifestyle_tips: Strictly avoid smoking and exposure to passive second-hand tobacco smoke.
Rest your voice and avoid speaking loudly in cold air.
Use an air purifier with a true HEPA filter in your sleeping area.
diagnostic_tests: Chest X-ray (only if high fever or hypoxia suggests pneumonia)
emergency_red_flags: Coughing up significant quantities of frank blood (Hemoptysis)
Fever above 101.5°F lasting more than 3-4 days
Severe breathlessness or resting oxygen saturation below 93%

name: Streptococcal Pharyngitis (Strep Throat)
overview: A bacterial throat infection caused by Group A Streptococcus that causes a severe, sudden sore throat without cough.
detailed_explanation: Streptococcal pharyngitis is caused by Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A beta-hemolytic strep).
