It causes acute exudative inflammation of the palatine tonsils and posterior pharynx. Unlike viral sore throats, Strep throat typically lacks cough, rhinorrhea, or conjunctivitis, and requires antibiotic treatment to prevent rheumatic fever and post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis.
causes_and_triggers: Infection with Streptococcus pyogenes bacteria
Direct respiratory droplet spread from coughing/sneezing
Sharing utensils, drinks, or kissing an infected person

medicines.name: Amoxicillin or Penicillin V
medicines.purpose: Antibiotic of choice to eradicate Streptococcus pyogenes and eliminate risk of acute rheumatic fever
medicines.instructions: Amoxicillin 500mg twice daily or 250mg three times daily for a strict 10-day course.
medicines.precautions: Must complete all 10 days even if throat pain vanishes within 48 hours.

medicines.name: Ibuprofen or Paracetamol
medicines.purpose: Relieves intense odynophagia (painful swallowing) and lowers fever
medicines.instructions: Ibuprofen 400 mg with food every 6-8 hours as needed.
medicines.precautions: Ensure hydration.

remedies.name: Warm Salt Water Gargling
remedies.description: Gargle 1/2 teaspoon of salt in warm water every 3 hours.
remedies.benefit: Physically draws out inflammatory fluid from swollen tonsillar tissues.

remedies.name: Sucking on Throat Lozenges / Ice Pops
remedies.description: Suck on benzocaine/menthol lozenges or fruit ice pops.
remedies.benefit: Temporarily numbs localized pharyngeal pain receptors, easing fluid swallowing.

recommended: Smooth lukewarm pureed soups and broths
Soft scrambled eggs, mashed potatoes, and yogurt
Cool smoothies (non-citrus) and applesauce
Chilled milk or plant milk
avoid: Crunchy, sharp foods: chips, crackers, raw vegetables
Acidic citrus juices (orange, grapefruit) and tomato sauce
Hot chili peppers and coarse spices

lifestyle_tips: Replace your toothbrush 24-48 hours after starting antibiotics to prevent re-infection.
Stay home from work or school until at least 24 hours after initiating antibiotic therapy and fever-free.
emergency_red_flags: Difficulty opening the mouth wide (Trismus) or severe unilateral throat bulge (Peritonsillar Abscess / Quinsy)
Drooling saliva or inability to swallow own saliva
Stridor (high-pitched gasping sound on breathing in)
Stiff neck or widespread sandpapery red rash (Scarlet fever)

name: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS)
overview: A common disorder characterized by abdominal pain, cramping, bloating, and changes in bowel habits without structural tissue damage.
detailed_explanation: IBS is a disorder of gut-brain interaction (DGBI) characterized by visceral hypersensitivity, altered gut motility, low-grade mucosal immune activation, and microbiome dysbiosis. Classified into IBS-D (diarrhea-predominant), IBS-C (constipation-predominant), or IBS-M (mixed).
causes_and_triggers: Dysregulation between central nervous system and enteric gut nervous system
Post-infectious sequelae following severe food poisoning
High-FODMAP carbohydrate malabsorption and bacterial fermentation
Chronic psychological distress, anxiety, and autonomic arousal

medicines.name: Mebeverine or Dicyclomine
medicines.purpose: Antispasmodic relaxing intestinal smooth muscle cramping and spasms
medicines.instructions: Take 20 minutes before meals as directed by doctor.
medicines.precautions: May cause dry mouth or blurred vision.

medicines.name: Psyllium Husk (Isabgol)
medicines.purpose: Soluble prebiotic fiber that regulates stool consistency in both constipation and diarrhea
medicines.instructions: 1 tablespoon in a full glass of water, followed immediately by a second glass of water.
medicines.precautions: Must drink plenty of fluid; avoid insoluble bran which worsens bloating.

medicines.name: Peppermint Oil Capsules (Enteric-coated)
medicines.purpose: Blocks calcium channels in smooth muscle, reducing painful colic and intestinal spasms
medicines.instructions: 1-2 capsules 30-60 minutes before meals on an empty stomach.
medicines.precautions: Must be enteric coated to prevent heartburn.

remedies.name: Low-FODMAP Dietary Protocol
remedies.description: Temporarily eliminate Fermentable Oligosaccharides, Disaccharides, Monosaccharides, and Polyols under dietetic guidance.
remedies.benefit: Reduces gas production, visceral distension, and osmotic diarrhea in up to 75% of patients.

remedies.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing & Gut-Directed Relaxation
remedies.description: Practice 10 minutes of deep abdominal breathing twice daily before meals.
remedies.benefit: Activates parasympathetic vagal tone, quelling intestinal hyper-reactivity.

recommended: Soluble fiber (oats, cooked carrots, zucchini)
Low-FODMAP fruits: bananas, blueberries, oranges
Lean proteins: chicken breast, eggs, tofu
Herbal peppermint or fennel teas
avoid: High-FODMAP foods: onions, garlic, wheat, apples, cauliflower, beans
Sorbitol, xylitol, and artificial sweeteners in sugar-free gums
Carbonated beverages, beer, and high caffeine
Greasy fried foods

lifestyle_tips: Eat at predictable, structured meal times without rushing.
Engage in regular moderate aerobic exercise like yoga, walking, or swimming.
Keep a food and symptom journal for 3 weeks to pinpoint trigger ingredients.
diagnostic_tests: Fecal Calprotectin (to rule out Crohn's/Ulcerative Colitis)
emergency_red_flags: Unexplained rapid weight loss
Rectal bleeding or black tarry stools
Nocturnal diarrhea awakening you from sleep (IBS rarely occurs during sleep)
Onset of new symptoms after age 50

name: Vertigo (Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo - BPPV)
overview: A sensation of spinning or whirling where the room feels like it is rotating, triggered by specific changes in head position.
detailed_explanation: BPPV occurs when microscopic calcium carbonate otoconia crystals (canaliths) dislodge from the utricle and migrate into one of the semicircular canals (most commonly the posterior canal) of the inner ear. When the head moves, these crystals cause abnormal endolymph fluid displacement, stimulating hair cells and generating an illusion of violent rotation and horizontal/torsional nystagmus.
causes_and_triggers: Dislodged calcium otoconia crystals in the inner ear semicircular canals
Minor head trauma or concussion
Prolonged recumbent position (e.g., at the dentist or hair salon)
Inner ear viral infection (vestibular neuritis) or aging

medicines.name: Betahistine
medicines.purpose: Improves inner ear microcirculation and reduces endolymphatic pressure
medicines.instructions: 8-16 mg three times daily with food as prescribed.
medicines.precautions: Caution in patients with bronchial asthma or peptic ulcer.

medicines.name: Meclizine or Dimenhydrinate
medicines.purpose: Vestibular suppressant antihistamine to alleviate acute spinning nausea
medicines.instructions: 25 mg orally as needed.
medicines.precautions: Causes significant drowsiness; do not drive. Should only be used for short durations as it delays central compensation.

remedies.name: The Epley Canalith Repositioning Maneuver
remedies.description: A precise 4-step sequence of head positions performed on a bed or by an audiologist/physician.
remedies.benefit: Physically guides displaced calcium crystals by gravity out of the semicircular canal back into the utricle, curing up to 90% of BPPV cases.

remedies.name: Brandt-Daroff Home Exercises
remedies.description: Sit upright, lie swiftly onto one side with head turned 45 degrees up, wait 30 seconds, sit up, repeat on opposite side.
remedies.benefit: Aids central vestibular compensation and breaks up canalith aggregates.

recommended: Consistent hydration with pure water throughout the day
Balanced meals preventing reactive hypoglycemia
Ginger tea to curb nausea
avoid: Excessive dietary sodium (causes fluid fluctuation in inner ear)
High caffeine and energy drinks that constrict microvessels
Alcohol, which alters inner ear fluid density and causes positional nystagmus

lifestyle_tips: Avoid sleeping completely flat; use two pillows to keep head elevated 30 degrees.
Turn your head slowly and avoid sudden backward head tilts (e.g. looking up at high shelves).
Sit on the edge of the bed for 1 minute before standing up in the morning.
diagnostic_tests: Brain MRI (to rule out posterior circulation stroke or acoustic neuroma)
emergency_red_flags: Vertigo accompanied by double vision, slurred speech, facial drooping, or arm weakness (STROKE - ACT F.A.S.T)
Sudden profound hearing loss in one ear
Inability to stand or sit unsupported (Truncal ataxia)
New severe occipital headache

name: Shingles (Herpes Zoster)
overview: A reactivation of the varicella-zoster virus causing a painful, blistering skin rash that typically follows a specific nerve pathway (dermatome).
detailed_explanation: Following a childhood chickenpox infection, the varicella-zoster virus (VZV) remains dormant within dorsal root ganglia. When cellular immunity wanes with age or immunosuppression, the virus reactivates, travels along sensory axons to the skin, causing severe burning nerve pain (neuropathic pain) followed by a unilateral band of clustered fluid-filled vesicles.
causes_and_triggers: Reactivation of dormant Varicella-Zoster Virus in sensory ganglia
Age over 50 years with declining cell-mediated immunity
Physical or severe emotional trauma/stress
Immunocompromising conditions or immunosuppressive therapy

medicines.name: Valacyclovir or Acyclovir (Antivirals)
medicines.purpose: Inhibits viral DNA polymerase, accelerating lesion crusting and dramatically reducing risk of Postherpetic Neuralgia (PHN)
medicines.instructions: Valacyclovir 1000 mg 3 times daily for 7 days. Must be initiated within 72 hours of rash onset for optimal outcome.
medicines.precautions: Drink plenty of water to prevent renal crystallization.

medicines.name: Gabapentin or Pregabalin
medicines.purpose: Modulates alpha-2-delta calcium subunit to calm excruciating neuropathic burning nerve pain
medicines.instructions: Titrated slowly by physician.
medicines.precautions: Causes dizziness and somnolence; do not stop abruptly.

medicines.name: Calamine Lotion / Topical Lidocaine Patch
medicines.purpose: Soothes raw dermatomal irritation and provides localized surface anesthesia
medicines.instructions: Apply calamine lotion to weeping blisters; apply lidocaine patch strictly to intact healed skin.
medicines.precautions: Never apply adhesive patches over open broken blisters.

remedies.name: Cool Saline Wet Compresses
remedies.description: Soak a sterile cloth in cool saline solution and drape gently over blisters for 20 minutes, 3 times daily.
remedies.benefit: Cools fiery burning pain and dries out weeping vesicles.

remedies.name: Colloidal Oatmeal Lukewarm Soaks
remedies.description: Take a 15-minute lukewarm bath with dissolved oatmeal powder.
remedies.benefit: Relieves itch and soothes inflamed cutaneous nerve endings.

recommended: High-Lysine foods (poultry, fish, yogurt, cheese) which counterbalance arginine
Vitamin B12 and Vitamin C rich foods for nerve myelin sheath support
Hydrating leafy greens, orange fruits, and plenty of water
avoid: High-Arginine foods (chocolate, peanuts, almonds, gelatin) which fuel herpes virus replication
Refined white sugar and fried junk food

lifestyle_tips: Wear loose, smooth 100% silk or modal cotton clothing to prevent friction over sensitive dermatomes.
Keep the blistering rash cleanly covered with non-stick sterile dressings to prevent spreading varicella to unvaccinated contacts.
Get the Shingrix recombinant shingles vaccine (recommended for all adults aged 50+).
diagnostic_tests: VZV PCR swab of blister fluid
emergency_red_flags: Rash appearing on the tip or side of the nose, or near the eye (Herpes Zoster Ophthalmicus - PERMANENT BLINDNESS RISK - IMMEDIATE OPHTHALMOLOGY EMERGENCY)
Severe facial weakness, ear pain, and loss of taste (Ramsay Hunt Syndrome)
Rash spreading widely over the entire body (Disseminated Zoster)

name: Conjunctivitis (Pink Eye)
overview: Inflammation or infection of the transparent membrane (conjunctiva) that lines the eyelid and covers the white part of the eyeball.
detailed_explanation: Conjunctivitis can be viral (Adenovirus, highly contagious), bacterial (Staphylococcus, Streptococcus), or allergic. It causes engorgement of the superficial conjunctival blood vessels, leading to prominent redness, foreign-body grittiness, and varying degrees of discharge.
causes_and_triggers: Viral infection (frequently accompanying a cold or adenovirus infection)
Bacterial contamination from unwashed fingers or expired makeup
Allergens (pollen, animal dander, dust mites)
Wearing contact lenses too long or improper contact lens disinfection

medicines.name: Artificial Tears (Carboxymethylcellulose / Hyaluronic Acid)
medicines.purpose: Flushes allergens and infectious debris while providing soothing lubrication
medicines.instructions: 1-2 drops in each eye 4-6 times daily as needed (preservative-free formulations preferred).
medicines.precautions: Do not touch dropper tip to eyeball or lashes to prevent contamination.

medicines.name: Moxifloxacin or Tobramycin Eye Drops
medicines.purpose: Antibacterial eye drop indicated strictly for bacterial conjunctivitis (thick yellow/green pus)
medicines.instructions: 1 drop every 4-6 hours for 5-7 days as prescribed.
medicines.precautions: Ineffective against viral pink eye; do not use indiscriminately.

medicines.name: Ketotifen or Olopatadine Eye Drops
medicines.purpose: Antihistamine mast-cell stabilizer for intense itchy allergic pink eye
medicines.instructions: 1 drop twice daily.
medicines.precautions: Remove contact lenses.

remedies.name: Cold / Warm Sterile Compresses
remedies.description: Apply a clean washcloth soaked in cool boiled water over closed eyelids for 5-10 minutes.
remedies.benefit: Reduces eyelid edema, relieves burning, and gently softens crusty exudates.

remedies.name: Eyelid Margin Cleansing
remedies.description: Wipe closed eyelids gently from inner corner to outer corner using disposable sterile saline wipes.
remedies.benefit: Removes crusted nocturnal secretions without reinfecting the ocular surface.

lifestyle_tips: STOP wearing contact lenses immediately until the infection has completely resolved and replace old lenses.
Throw away all mascara, eyeliner, and eye creams used since infection onset.
Do not share towels, washcloths, or pillows with family members.
diagnostic_tests: Fluorescein Staining (to rule out corneal abrasion/ulcer)
emergency_red_flags: Severe deep eye pain (indicative of acute angle-closure glaucoma or uveitis)
Significant decrease in vision that does not clear when blinking
Extreme sensitivity to light (Photophobia)
Pupil of the affected eye is irregular or fixed
